text:
we are fundamentally constrained by the architecture of our own minds and experiences. If a concept is entirely foreign to everything in our reality, we literally lack the neurological framework or sensory vocabulary to even conceive of it—it would be like trying to imagine a completely new color that has never existed.

At the same time, because our imagination is built from the raw building blocks of the universe we inhabit, anything our minds *can* construct is ultimately anchored in those rules, even if it feels sci-fi or abstract right now. It is all just permutations of reality waiting to be unlocked or proven.

Do you think human imagination is a hard ceiling on what can exist, or is it just a tiny window looking out at a vast landscape of physics and matter that we haven't even begun to stumble across yet?
